records.label: Proband (30-year-old woman)

phenotypes.text: annular and polycyclic erythematous hyperkeratotic plaques on trunk and extremities that resolved
interrupted perinuclear tonofilament rings on electron microscopy

quotes: A 30-year-old white woman developed bullous and ichthyosiform skin lesions at the age of 8 months. Blistering ceased at puberty, but the hyperkeratotic plaques persisted.
At the age of 27 years, she developed numerous annular and polycyclic, erythematous, hyperkeratotic plaques on the trunk and extremities that were pruritic, enlarged slowly, and then resolved.

Electron microscopic examination of the annular plaques showed interrupted perinuclear tonofilament rings consistent with either bullous ichthyotic erythroderma of Brocq or ichthyosis bullosa of Siemens.

quotes: She subsequently delivered five children, two of whom were affected with a bullous type of ichthyosis.

records.label: Family with two affected generations

phenotypes.text: episodic annular and polycyclic erythematous hyperkeratotic plaques on trunk and proximal extremities
abnormal keratin filament networks with perinuclear tonofilament clumping

variants.as_reported: tandem CG to GA 2-bp mutation ... arginine to glutamate substitution at residue 83 (R83E) of the 2B helical segment

records.segregation: found in affected individuals of two generations
quotes: Here we report a second incidence of this disorder in a family with two affected generations.

The proband suffered from bullous ichthyosis and had bouts of disease activity associated with the development of numerous annular and polycyclic erythematous, hyperkeratotic plaques on the trunk and the proximal extremities.

Molecular analysis revealed a novel tandem CG to GA 2-bp mutation in the same allele of keratin 10 in affected individuals, resulting in an arginine to glutamate substitution at residue 83 (R83E) of the 2B helical segment.
records.genotype_reason: single heterozygous variant; mode as stated for the family

records.label: Third kindred with annular epidermolytic ichthyosis

phenotypes.text: hyperkeratotic lichenified plaques in flexural areas and extensor surfaces
intermittent annular and polycyclic erythematous scaly plaques on trunk and proximal extremities

variants.as_reported: isoleucine to threonine substitution at residue 107 (codon 446)

quotes: We now describe a third kindred with annular epidermolytic ichthyosis.

Molecular analysis of this family revealed a novel mutation resulting in an isoleucine to threonine substitution at residue 107 (codon 446) within the highly conserved helix termination motif at the end of the rod domain of keratin 10.

records.label: 8-year-old girl

phenotypes.text: erythematous scaly hyperkeratotic plaques with prominent borders
yellowish hyperkeratotic plaques on scalp and nasal introitus

quotes: An 8-year-old female patient was attended at the pediatric dermatology outpatient clinic of the Hospital Santa Casa of Porto Alegre with a report of diffuse dermatosis that began in the first months of life.

Upon examination, the patient presented erythematous, scaly, hyperkeratotic plaques with prominent borders, affecting the mesogastrium, cubital fossae, popliteal fossae, and inguinal and cervical regions, as well as palmoplantar hyperkeratosis and yellowish hyperkeratotic plaques on the scalp and nasal introitus
Skin biopsy in the extensor portion of the forearm showed acanthosis, papillomatosis, and hyperkeratosis with marked epidermolysis in the granular layer (Fig. 4).

notes.statement: Mikilita et al. (2020) reviewed the literature published in English, Portuguese, and Spanish after the first description by Sahn et al. (1992). They found 19 cases of annular epidermolytic ichthyosis in 10 publications.
quotes: The present authors have reviewed the literature published in English, Portuguese, and Spanish since its description and found 19 cases in 10 publications that are summarized in table 1.

notes.statement: Mikilita et al. (2020) noted that the main differential diagnosis of annular epidermolytic ichthyosis is erythrokeratodermia variabilis et progressiva (EKVP). EKVP is distinguished by onset during childhood, the absence of epidermal fragility, and histology without epidermolysis. In their patient, the initial diagnosis of EKVP was revised after biopsy showed epidermolytic hyperkeratosis.
quotes: The main differential diagnosis of annular epidermolytic ichthyosis is with erythrokeratodermia variabilis et progressiva (EKVP),
Distinctive features of EKVP include onset during childhood, absence of epidermal fragility, and histology without evidence of epidermolysis.

The initial hypothesis was erythrokeratodermia variabilis et progressiva; however, the finding of epidermolytic hyperkeratosis in histopathological examination led to the diagnosis of annular epidermolytic ichthyosis.

notes.statement: In their literature review, Mikilita et al. (2020) found that topical treatments, including retinoids, corticosteroids, propylene glycol, calcipotriene, and keratolytics, produced little response. Three reports described a good response to systemic retinoids (acitretin, or low-dose isotretinoin).
quotes: Treatment options in the small number of patients reported included topical medications such as retinoids, topical corticosteroids, propylene glycol, calcipotriene, and keratolytic agents, and little response was observed.,,, Three articles report good response with systemic retinoids; two articles cite acitretin treatment with good response, and another reports good response with low doses of isotretinoin.

notes.statement: Suga et al. (1998) described annular epidermolytic ichthyosis as a distinct phenotypic variant of bullous congenital ichthyosiform erythroderma, in which bullous ichthyosis in early childhood is followed by hyperkeratotic lichenified plaques in flexural and extensor areas, with characteristic intermittent bouts of annular and polycyclic erythematous scaly plaques on the trunk and proximal extremities.
quotes: Annular epidermolytic ichthyosis is a distinct phenotypic variant of bullous congenital ichthyosiform erythroderma that has recently been described in two separate kindreds.
Characteristically, they also develop intermittent bouts of annular and polycyclic, erythematous, scaly plaques on the trunk and proximal extremities.

notes.statement: Joh et al. (1997) stated that the inheritance pattern of annular epidermolytic ichthyosis was consistent with autosomal dominant transmission.
quotes: The pattern of inheritance of the disorder is consistent with an autosomal dominant mode of transmission.

notes.statement: Joh et al. (1997) concluded that annular epidermolytic ichthyosis should be considered a variant of bullous congenital ichthyosiform erythroderma.
quotes: We conclude that annular epidermolytic ichthyosis should be considered a variant of bullous congenital ichthyosiform erythroderma.

notes.statement: Sahn et al. (1992) suggested that a kindred in which a mother developed annular, polycyclic, erythematous hyperkeratotic plaques that resolved, and which showed epidermolytic hyperkeratosis on histology, may represent a new phenotype of epidermolytic (acanthokeratolytic) ichthyosis.
quotes: This kindred may represent a new phenotype of epidermolytic (acanthokeratolytic) ichthyosis.
Histopathologic examination of these annular plaques revealed epidermolytic hyperkeratosis.
